why: Adding (1+1)^n = 2^n and (1-1)^n = 0 gives 2*(sum of even-index binomials) = 2^n, so the sum is 2^(n-1); verified numerically for n = 2,4,6,8,10 (2, 8, 32, 128, 512).

n(n+1)...(n+r-1)/r! = C(n+r-1, r), an integer, so r consecutive integers always have product divisible by r!. Note (r-1)! also divides it as a weaker consequence, but r! is the standard/maximal guaranteed divisor and (r+1)! fails (e.g. r=2: 1*2=2 is not divisible by 6).

T_(3r) has coefficient C(2n, 3r-1) and T_(r+2) has C(2n, r+1); equality needs 3r-1 = r+1 (giving only r = 1) or (3r-1)+(r+1) = 2n, i.e. 4r = 2n, n = 2r. Checked: n=6, r=3 gives C(12,8) = C(12,4) = 495.
In an A.P. a1+a4 = a2+a3 = 10, so a2, a3 are roots of t^2 - 10t + 24 = 0, i.e. 4 and 6; the A.P. is 2, 4, 6, 8 (or its reverse), whose least term is 2.
19(a+11d) = 18(a+10d) gives 19a + 209d = 18a + 180d, so a + 29d = 0, and a + 29d is exactly the 30th term.

Ratio of the m-th terms equals the sum ratio evaluated at n = 2m-1; for m = 13 that is n = 25, giving (2*25+3)/(6*25+5) = 53/155. Verified by constructing S1 = n(2n+3), S2 = n(6n+5) and differencing: a13 = 53 and 155.

value: y = 2xz/(x+z), i.e. x, y, z in H.P.
why: (x+z)(x+z-2y) = (x-z)^2 expands to (x+z)^2 - (x-z)^2 = 2y(x+z), i.e. 4xz = 2y(x+z), so y is the harmonic mean of x and z; checked with x=2, z=8 giving y=3.2 and 1/2, 1/3.2, 1/8 in A.P.

Rationalising, the k-th term is +/-(sqrt(k+1)+sqrt(k)) for k = 9..120 with + for odd k; the alternating sums telescope to sqrt(9) - sqrt(121) = 3 - 11 = -8. Confirmed at 60-digit precision (residual ~1e-57).
[(1/2)(A - A')]' = (1/2)(A' - A) = -(1/2)(A - A'), which is exactly the skew-symmetry condition.
Exhaustive search over all 2^9 = 512 matrices with 0/1 entries gives maximum determinant 2, attained e.g. by rows (0,1,1), (1,0,1), (1,1,0).

value: a number associated to a square matrix
why: A determinant is a scalar, not a matrix (kills A), and it is defined only for square matrices (kills B, which omits 'square'); hence C, and D fails since A and B are wrong.

The matrix is Hermitian (each a_ij = conj(a_ji), verified), so its determinant is real; exact evaluation gives z = -145. C fails since z + conj(z) = -290 is nonzero; D reduces to 0*i = 0, which is not normally called purely imaginary.
For skew-symmetric M of odd order n=3, det(M) = det(M') = det(-M) = (-1)^3 det(M) = -det(M), so 2 det(M) = 0 and det(M) = 0.
|A^2013 - 3A^2012| = |A^2012||A - 3I| = (-1)^2012 * (-7) = -7; verified by exact integer 2x2 fast exponentiation of A to the 2013th and 2012th powers.

The collinearity determinant factors as a^2 (t1 - t2)(2 t1 t2 - t1 - t2); since the points are distinct, t1 != t2, forcing 2 t1 t2 = t1 + t2. Numerically, t1=3, t2=3/5 gives zero area while t1 t2 = 1 and t1 t2 = -1 do not.
If A is symmetric and invertible, (A^-1)' = (A')^-1 = A^-1, so the inverse is symmetric.

value: both statements true; Statement-2 not the correct explanation
why: For 2x2 matrices adj(adj A) = A identically and |adj A| = |A|^(n-1) = |A|, both verified over 2000 random integer matrices, so both statements are true. Statement-1 follows from the general adj(adj A) = |A|^(n-2) A specialised at n=2 rather than from Statement-2, which is the standard key's reading; a case can be made for D, since adj(adj A)*adj A = |adj A| I = |A| I = A*adj A does use Statement-2 for invertible A.

For x20 to be the middle (3rd smallest) of 5 picks, exactly 2 must come from the 19 smaller values x1..x19 and 2 from the 30 larger x21..x50; option B is 30C2 * 19C2, the same product. Brute-force checks on smaller analogues (N=10 and N=12) matched the formula exactly.
There are 5 even tickets among 10, so the probability is C(5,2)/C(10,2) = 10/45 = 2/9.
